transformations: clean-workspace and five-callouts: decode the palette PNG to RGB; uniform scale 800x600 -> 1200x900 (exactly 1.5x on both axes, no aspect rounding) with Pillow Image.Resampling.BOX, chosen after comparing NEAREST (uneven 1/2-px strokes in pixel text), LANCZOS (softer, faint ringing) and BOX (even, crisp strokes); embed at x=347, y=90 (1:1 device pixels).

side-by-side: no resampling. The HIST-02 PNG bytes are embedded unchanged, drawn 1:1 at x=127, y=156 (clean, left) and x=976, y=156 (annotated, right). 1.0x is the largest scale at which both whole screenshots, their frames, gutters and rails fit the 1680 px safe width; it also keeps every pixel of the pixel fonts original.
Every placement sits inside a 6 px #1b2027 mat and 2 px #343d48 stroke drawn entirely outside the image edges on the #111318 background.
clean-workspace and the left screenshot of side-by-side: nothing else. five-callouts and the right screenshot of side-by-side: annotation marks listed below; labels outside the screenshots.
No crop, rotation, stretch, retouch, colour change, dimming, zoom-in, watermark removal or partial use in any variant.
authored_additions: Labels: the five War/SCRIPT.md:133 cue strings (Form Designer, Toolbox, Properties Window, Code Window, Project Window), Liberation Sans Bold 40 px, #f1f3f5. five-callouts: side margins outside the screenshot and its frame, multi-word labels stacked one word per line (left column right-aligned at x=291: Toolbox, Form Designer, Code Window; right column from x=1603: Project Window, Properties Window). side-by-side: one line each in a strip below the annotated screenshot (rows at y 777-931), left group starting x=1000 (Code Window, Form Designer, Toolbox), right group ending x=1752 (Properties Window, Project Window).

five-callouts outlines and leaders: 5 px thick (1 px #111318 casing, 3 px #eab676 core, 1 px casing); outlines inside each target window's outer boundary (about 3.3 original px, the frame bevel); horizontal leaders over desktop teal; the Form Designer outline stops 6 px short of the Code Window outline.

side-by-side outlines and leaders: 4 px thick (1 px casing, 2 px gold core, 1 px casing) so each outline covers only the 4 px Win95 outer window frame at 1.0x; each leader is an exit segment over desktop teal (original rows leader_y-2 .. leader_y+1) to the image edge, a vertical rail in the dark gutter (left rails at x 942/952/962 for Toolbox/Form Designer/Code Window; right rails at x 1786/1796 for Properties Window/Project Window), and a run below the screenshot to its label. The Form Designer outline stops 5 px short of the Code Window outline.
src/build.py, src/verify.py, src/finalize.py: deterministic authoring (labels read from the script cue), pixel verification and delivery finishing.

producer_decisions.source: Render Lane Manager hand-off (session vb-97), original production
decisions: Whole 800x600 screenshot, uniform scale, no crop/rotation/stretch/retouch/zoom in both variants; pixel-verify the clean image region.
Label text outside the screenshot; only thin leaders/outlines may cross onto it; record every mark as annotation edit history.

Keep the five labels verbatim, including 'Project Explorer'; raise Project Explorer vs Project window for the Writing Lead; no UI painted to fit a label. (Superseded for the fifth label by Devin's 2026-09-15 ruling below.)
Carry HIST-02 credit/rights forward; 'Used with permission from Microsoft' is proposed only; release blocked on R14 (and R03); never in a cleared-media bin.
Work R03 against the screenshot layout; a mismatch becomes a review question, not a script edit.

producer_decisions.source: Devin (project author), rulings of 2026-09-15 relayed by the Render Lane Manager (session vb-8c)
decisions: Q1: callout marks over the Microsoft screenshot are allowed; keep the outline and leader treatment; no fallback.

Q2: the fifth label is 'Project Window' per War/SCRIPT.md:133 (writing change); build.py reads the five labels from the script cue and asserts exactly five. 'Form Designer' and its VB6-era note unchanged (Writing Lead item).
Q3 (narration) routed to the Writing Lead and Q4 (credit placement) routed to the producer; no art change.
Q5: research the Loan project's authorship; only an unresolved or third-party result stays a review question; the research does not clear release.

Q6: add a named side-by-side variant (clean left, annotated right, whole, same uniform scale, filling the safe width, label text off the image); decide the poster from the 720p review; keep clean-workspace and five-callouts.
